label: survey-20261125
question: From reports/MEGAKERNEL-SQUID5090-SURVEY-20261125.md: (S) do the sampled-draft modes Strata v0.2.17 already has make Pi-sampled long-context decode faster; (K) which of six never-measured knobs documented as bit-identical are bit-identical on the 4090 and faster; (M) how much does one graph node, and a 20 us delay before the doorbell or after the resident experts, add to the window?
decision_owner: the user; S and K are production env changes and need the user's confirmation
verdict_note: verdict_kind approx only so that `upgrade_gate.py approx` runs the KL block; replay --eval is NOT used for this label. The verdict is tools/upgrade_gate/survey_eval.py, whose sha256 is in SURVEY_EVAL.sha256 beside this file on the 4090, written before the first replay run.

identity.upgrade_gate: sha256 in ADDENDUM.json (frozen before the first run)

kl.yardstick: quant_quality.py run --gpu-experts auto on the production config, as in V0217-TAILSKIP-KL: expert cache filled from the profile, no adaptation, 5 segments x 999 positions; compared with the stored runs auto-ts0-a (exact routing) and auto-ts7 (B2)
kl.bitwise_rule: a K knob is BITWISE when its KL against the stored B2 run is 0 and top-1 1.0 (kl_vs_b2 == 0, top1_vs_b2 == 1). Only BITWISE knobs get replay runs; the others are recorded as NOT_BITWISE and leave this lossless group

workload.requests: one per assistant message k: messages[:k]; 120 in all (A 71, B 49)
workload.body: model, messages, tools = pisim TOOLS, max_tokens 16384, stream false, seed 20261123 + request index (0-based)
workload.history: fixed: recorded messages, never the arm's own replies; replies are measured and discarded
workload.estimate_method: A prompts as recorded; B prompts = A last prompt + A last completion (61806) + B prompt - 506
limits: fixed history makes the engine re-read the recorded reply each step (hundreds to a few thousand tokens), Pi reuses its own
pisim system prompt about 800 tokens and 4 tools; no streaming, no NGINX; one session, no switching

schedule: phase 1: runs 1-17 in order (K runs skipped when not BITWISE). phase 2 (confirmation): the b-run of every S or K arm whose screen gain is positive, in the order listed, then C5. All runs carry STRATA_SPEC_DEPTH=1 (acceptance by draft depth, print only). MLP / MLH run on the v0.2.17-xp build (its identity is the xp KL run off).

rules.metric: engine decode tok/s over the requests with prompt >= 32K (ge32k.decode_tok_s); ms per window and tokens per window recorded
rules.noise: aa = (max - min) / mean of decode tok/s over the valid controls (C1-C4 in phase 1; C1-C5 for the final verdict)
rules.bar: max(0.022, 2 * aa): SpecPilot adoption rule 1% + 2 x noise with the 0.6% ABBA noise of b2-adapt-long, raised when this session is noisier
rules.screen: gain1 = run / mean(the two controls bracketing it) - 1; confirm when gain1 > 0
rules.pass: mean of the arm's two runs / mean of all valid controls - 1 >= bar, AND each of the two runs is above the mean of all controls, AND (S arms) finish=length and repeat notices each <= max over controls + 1, AND (K arms) BITWISE
rules.m_runs: MD8: per-node cost = (MD8 ms_win - mean(C3, C4) ms_win) / (8 x 48); MLP / MLH: slope = delta ms_win / (0.020 ms x 48), against mean(C3, C4); MPF: the per-request stage split, structure only (the profiler changes the graph)
rules.cotenant: recorded for every run; a run with co-tenant mean > 4.5 cores (above the container cap) is invalid and rerun once
rules.invalid: upgrade_gate replay validity checks; an invalid run is rerun once (--rerun)

limits: the OCR container (CPU-only, capped at 4 cores) was busy at 2-4 cores when this was written; controls are interleaved and aa reflects it

S arms change sampled text: their decode tok/s compares different texts, hence two runs each; COUPLED keeps the target sampler, GUMBEL and PROB+top keep the target distribution, so no quality gate (Strata unit tests are not run in this round)
KL covers prompt-read windows only (head sampling off); K knobs that act only in sampled decode are not seen there
STRATA_SELECT_LONG is left out (only >= 64K, second graph set, VRAM)
